judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled, full per-app schema validation (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, googleCredentialSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) is discarded in favor of the broken minimum schema, so garbage or malformed token payloads are accepted whenever they contain an access_token. A credential-sync endpoint returning malformed data (missing instance_url for Salesforce, expiry_date for Google, etc.) passes validation, corrupt credentials get persisted via prisma.credential.update, and subsequent API calls fail in provider-specific ways instead of being rejected at refresh time — validation weakened on the sync path with no requirement justifying it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, ignores the passed per-app Zod schema and instead validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). That is a clear weakening of validation on the “credential sharing/sync enabled” path. Additionally, the “minimum” schema is itself incorrectly constructed using computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, so it does not actually express “any numeric expiry field” and will behave unexpectedly. This combination can let invalid/partial token shapes bypass the intended per-provider schema checks on the sharing-enabled path and then be used to update stored credentials in refresh flows.
